Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    India (with secondary focus on US monetary policy)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    Indian equities rebounded after four sessions of losses, driven by softening US rate hike expectations following dovish commentary from Fed Governor Waller. Markets repriced the probability of a September Fed hike down to ~50% from ~63%. Capital market stocks surged on SEBI's signal to revise derivatives settlement mechanics. IT stocks and broader indices gained modestly. Brent crude also firmed, adding a residual headwind.

Q01. Is the content's main message on the US economy, US yields, US interest rates?
Relevance: YES (US rate policy is the primary catalyst cited for the market move, though the article's geographic focus is India)

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 45 (partially — a September hike remains on the table but expectations are fading)
Probability of increase: 50%

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 60 (Waller's dovish signal and softening inflation narrative lean toward a hold)
Probability of holding: 50%

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (no discussion of cuts; context is hike vs. hold only)
Probability of decrease: 0%

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: What is the sentiment/tone including the very latest information on US interest rates?
Sentiment: -45 (Noticeably more dovish than before — hike probability dropped sharply from 63% to 50%, driven by Waller's explicit support for a pause if inflation data cooperates)
